arxiv-1706-09159.title: Invariant submanifolds of ( L ​ C ​ S ) n (LCS)_{n} -Manifolds with respect to quarter symmetric metric connection
arxiv-1706-09159.creator: SHYAMAL KUMAR HUI, LAURIAN-IOAN PISCORAN and TANUMOY PAL
arxiv-1706-09159.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by SHYAMAL KUMAR HUI, LAURIAN-IOAN PISCORAN and TANUMOY PAL. The object of the present paper is to study invariant submanifolds of ( L ​ C ​ S ) n (LCS)_{n} -manifolds with respect to quarter symmetric metric connection. It is shown that the mean curvature of an invariant submanifold of ( L ​ C ​ S ) n (LCS)_{n} -manifold with respect to quarter symmetric metric connection and Levi-Civita connection are equal. An example is constructed to illustrate the results of the paper.

arxiv-1707-00456.title: Novel Approaches to Spectral Properties of Correlated Electron Materials: From Generalized Kohn-Sham Theory to Screened Exchange Dynamical Mean Field Theory
arxiv-1707-00456.creator: Pascal Delange 1, Steffen Backes 1, Ambroise van Roekeghem 2, Leonid Pourovskii 1,3, Hong Jiang 4, and Silke Biermann 1,3,5
arxiv-1707-00456.description: Abstract The most intriguing properties of emergent materials are typically consequences of highly correlated quantum states of their electronic degrees of freedom. Describing those materials from first principles remains a challenge for modern condensed matter theory. Here, we review, apply and discuss novel approaches to spectral properties of correlated electron materials, assessing current day predictive capabilities of electronic structure calculations.

arxiv-2106-11166.creator: Avinash Sharma, Radu Horaud, Diana Mateus
arxiv-2106-11166.description: Abstract Abstract In this book chapter we address the problem of 3D shape registration and we propose a novel technique based on spectral graph theory and probabilistic matching. Recent advancement in shape acquisition technology has led to the capture of large amounts of 3D data.

arxiv-2201-02548.title: Origin of the Large Entropy Change in the Molecular Caloric and Ferroelectric Ammonium Sulfate
arxiv-2201-02548.creator: Shurong Yuan, Bernet E. Meijer, Guanqun Cai, Richard J. C. Dixey, Franz Demmel, Martin T. Dove, Jiaxun Liu, Helen Y. Playford, Helen C. Walker, Anthony E. Phillips
arxiv-2201-02548.description: Abstract The deceptively simple inorganic salt ammonium sulfate undergoes a ferroelectric phase transition associated with a very large entropy change and both electrocaloric and barocaloric functionality. While the structural origins of the electrical polarisation are now well established, those of the entropy change have been controversial for over fifty years.

arxiv-2202-05942.title: Broadband polarization insensitivity and high detection efficiency in high-fill-factor superconducting microwire single-photon detectors
arxiv-2202-05942.creator: Dileep V. Reddy, Negar Otrooshi, Sae Woo Nam, Richard P. Mirin, Varun B. Verma
arxiv-2202-05942.description: Abstract Single-photon detection via absorption in current-biased nanoscale superconducting structures has become a preferred technology in quantum optics and related fields. Single-mode fiber packaged devices have seen new records set in detection efficiency, timing jitter, recovery times, and largest sustainable count rates.

arxiv-2210-11663.title: InfraRed Investigation in Singapore (IRIS) Observatory: Urban heat island contributors and mitigators analysis using neighborhood-scale thermal imaging Journal: Energy and Buildings
arxiv-2210-11663.creator: Miguel Martin 1 , Vasantha Ramani 1 , Clayton Miller 2,∗
arxiv-2210-11663.description: Abstract This paper studies heat fluxes from contributors and mitigators of urban heat islands using thermal images and weather data. Thermal images were collected by a rooftop observatory between November 2021 and April 2022. Over the same period, weather stations were operating at several locations on a university campus in Singapore.

arxiv-2302-03112.title: Family dispute: do Type IIP supernova siblings agree on their distance?
arxiv-2302-03112.creator: G. Csörnyei, C. Vogl, S. Taubenberger, A. Flörs, S. Blondin, M. G. Cudmani, A. Holas, S. Kressierer, B. Leibundgut, W. Hillebrandt
arxiv-2302-03112.description: Abstract Context. Type II supernovae provide a direct way to estimate distances through the expanding photosphere method, which is independent of the cosmic distance ladder. A recently introduced Gaussian process-based method allows for a fast and precise modelling of spectral time series, which puts accurate and computationally cheap Type II-based absolute distance determinations within reach. Aims.

arxiv-2312-13565.title: Automatic Curriculum Learning with Gradient Reward Signals
arxiv-2312-13565.creator: Ryan Campbell, Junsang Yoon
arxiv-2312-13565.description: Abstract \vskip-12.0pt This study 1 1 1 https://github.com/riensou/automatic_curriculum_learning explores an approach to Automatic Curriculum Learning (ACL) in reinforcement learning (RL), focusing on the integration of gradient norm reward signals. Traditional ACL methods primarily rely on predefined metrics that may not adequately capture the intricacies of learning dynamics.

arxiv-2404-03614.title: Towards Trustworthy Automated Program Verifiers: Formally Validating Translations into an Intermediate Verification Language (extended version)
arxiv-2404-03614.creator: Gaurav Parthasarathy, Thibault Dardinier, Benjamin Bonneau, Peter Müller, Alexander J. Summers
arxiv-2404-03614.description: Abstract . Automated program verifiers are typically implemented using an intermediate verification language (IVL), such as Boogie or Why3. A verifier front-end translates the input program and specification into an IVL program, while the back-end generates proof obligations for the IVL program and employs an SMT solver to discharge them.

arxiv-2404-18157.title: Unitarity implications of F ~ μ ​ ν \tilde{F}_{\mu\nu} and F μ ​ ν F_{\mu\nu} models with Lorentz invariance violation in e + ​ e − → μ + ​ μ − e^{+}e^{-}\rightarrow\mu^{+}\mu^{-}
arxiv-2404-18157.creator: Alessio T. B. Celeste, Adriano M. Santos
arxiv-2404-18157.description: Abstract We studied two different models that included Lorentz Invariance Violation coupling in the scattering processes of e + ​ e − → μ + ​ μ − e^{+}e^{-}\rightarrow\mu^{+}\mu^{-} . We found that using the model with the dual electromagnetic tensor F ~ μ ​ ν \tilde{F}_{\mu\nu} resulted in violations of unitarity in both vector and axial scenarios.

arxiv-2405-18651.title: A semi-analytical thermal model for craters with application to the crater-induced YORP effect
arxiv-2405-18651.creator: Wen-Han Zhou, Patrick Michel
arxiv-2405-18651.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Wen-Han Zhou, Patrick Michel. The YORP effect is the thermal torque generated by radiation from the surface of an asteroid. The effect is sensitive to surface topology, including small-scale roughness, boulders, and craters. The aim of this paper is to develop a computationally efficient semi-analytical model for the crater-induced YORP (CYORP) effect that can be used to investigate the functional dependence of this effect.

arxiv-2411-16571.title: Pantograph: A Fluid and Typed Structure Editor
arxiv-2411-16571.creator: Jacob Prinz, Henry Blanchette, Leonidas Lampropoulos
arxiv-2411-16571.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jacob Prinz, Henry Blanchette, Leonidas Lampropoulos. Structure editors operate directly on a program’s syntactic tree structure. At first glance, this allows for the exciting possibility that such an editor could enforce correctness properties: programs could be well-formed and sometimes even well-typed by construction. Unfortunately, traditional approaches to structure editing that attempt to rigidly enforce these properties face a seemingly fundamental problem, known in the literature as viscosity .

arxiv-2412-12662.title: Light-induced thermal noise anomaly governed by quantum metric
arxiv-2412-12662.creator: Longjun Xiang, Lei Zhang, Jun Chen, Fuming Xu, Yadong Wei, Jian Wang
arxiv-2412-12662.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Longjun Xiang, Lei Zhang, Jun Chen, Fuming Xu, Yadong Wei, Jian Wang. Traditionally, thermal noise in electric currents, arising from thermal agitation, is expected to increase with temperature T T and disappear as T T approaches zero. Contrary to this expectation, we discover that the resonant DC thermal noise (DTN) in photocurrents not only persists at T = 0 T=0 but also exhibits a divergence proportional to 1 / T 1/T .

arxiv-2506-04771.title: Integrated photonics for continuous-variable quantum optics
arxiv-2506-04771.creator: Rachel N. Clark, Bethany Puzio, Oliver M. Green, Siva T. Pradyumna, Oliver Trojak, Alberto Politi, Jonathan C. F. Matthews
arxiv-2506-04771.description: Abstract Quantum technologies promise profound advances in communication security, sensing and computing. The underpinning hardware must be engineered to generate, manipulate and detect quantum phenomena with exceptional performance, whilst being mass-manufacturable for real-world applications. A leading approach is chip-scale quantum photonics.

pmc-10616962.creator: Xiangqing Ren, Xiaolong Tang, Tian Huang, Zenan Hu, Yuping Wang, Yongning Zhou
pmc-10616962.description: Gastrointestinal cancer is a common malignancy with high mortality and poor prognosis. Accumulating studies have reported that N6-methyladenosine is the most abundant epigenetic modification in eukaryotes.

pmc-11485019.title: Assessment of ventilatory functions and associated inflammatory markers among workers in slaughterhouses
pmc-11485019.creator: Mona Abdallah Ramadan, Rateba said Mohammed, Aisha Safwat Saif Eldin
pmc-11485019.description: ObjectiveMeat processing is among the most extensive industries globally. However, data on the effects of occupational exposure on the pulmonary health of slaughterhouse workers is limited. Ascertaining the impact of the slaughterhouse atmosphere on the breathing habits of laborers exposed to it and the inflammatory markers associated with it was the aim of the current investigation.

pmc-12534477.title: Prevalence and drug resistance profiles of nontuberculous mycobacteria isolated from Iranian fish pond waters
pmc-12534477.creator: Xiaoqian Cui, Yu Zhang, Yancui Cai, Sale Zhang, Ying Li, Haifang Wang, Fatemeh Sakhaee, Seyed Davar Siadat, Abolfazl Fateh
pmc-12534477.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) infection is considered one of the most severe waterborne diseases. NTMs are widespread in fish pond water, which may serve as a significant exposure pathway for NTM infections, raising substantial concerns for public health. Consequently, the purpose of this study was to investigate the presence of NTM and determine their drug resistance in 120 fish pond waters (FPW). Totally, 120 water samples were gathered from FPW.

pmc-13051841.title: Barriers Implementing Patient‐Specific 3D‐Printed Bone Scaffolds in Australia: A Scoping Review
pmc-13051841.creator: Anthony Vidler, Angus Hayes, Srijoni Sengupta
pmc-13051841.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). 3D printing has emerged as an innovative technology over the last decade, with widespread uptake in several fields spanning science, technology and engineering; however, penetration into medical markets has been met with a variety of obstacles. At the 17th Global Conference on Sustainable Manufacturing in 2018, medical technology stakeholders held a workshop to discuss the barriers that hinder the widespread adoption and diffusion of 3D printing technology in the Australian medical field.

pmc-13455463.title: Gsformer: a dual-architecture deep learning framework with CNN-self-attention and sparse-attention for genomic selection
pmc-13455463.creator: Tingting Yang, Weicong Wu, Yahui Xue, Lei Zhou, Huimin Kang, Jianfeng Liu
pmc-13455463.description: BackgroundGenomic selection (GS) has revolutionized modern breeding by utilizing genome-wide single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). While traditional models such as GBLUP and Bayesian approaches remain prevalent, several deep learning approaches have recently been introduced for plant GS, demonstrating superior predictive performance. Here, we introduce Gsformer, a novel deep learning framework designed to predict phenotypes by modeling complex genetic architectures.

pmc-13469244.title: An Energy-Efficient Hybrid LoRa–Wi-Fi Architecture for Real- Time Water Quality Monitoring and Machine Learning-Based Trend Forecasting
pmc-13469244.creator: Jeya Sutha Mariadhason, Emerson Raja Joseph, Purushothaman Srinivasan, Ramesh Dhanaseelan Francis
pmc-13469244.description: Water quality management in large-scale institutional infrastructures faces significant challenges due to the high latency of manual sampling and the energy–connectivity trade-offs in traditional IoT deployments. This paper proposes HydroSense AI, a robust three-tier IoT framework designed for real-time multi-parameter water quality monitoring and predictive analytics.

pmc-13688355.title: Glucose Management in Children Living with Type 1 Diabetes: Results from the BETTER Registry
pmc-13688355.creator: Virginie Messier, Mélanie Henderson, Meranda Nakhla, Judith Simoneau-Roy, Meryem Talbo, Domitille Dervaux, Nathalie Kinnard, Andréane Vanasse, Monia Rekik, Rémi Rabasa-Lhoret, Anne-Sophie Brazeau, on behalf of the BETTER research group
pmc-13688355.description: IntroductionThe Behaviors, Therapies, Technologies, and Hypoglycemic Risk in Type 1 Diabetes (BETTER) Registry collects patient-reported outcomes and experiences on individuals living with type 1 diabetes in Canada. The objective of our study was to describe the management of type 1 diabetes reported by parents of children and young adolescents (<14 years of age) enrolled in the BETTER registry.
